title: Introduce a structured logger (replace console.error, add server-fn error logging)
description: Recurring 'no logger yet' gap flagged across reviews: src/db/client.ts pool 'error' handler console.error dumps the full pg client object (noisy in e2e output); P1 review flagged server-function handlers log nothing and env-validation errors lack context. Add a small structured logger, replace the console.error in db/client with logged error.message, and add log-and-rethrow at the server-fn boundary for observability.
design: Logger library: pino + pino-pretty (chosen after sweeping pino/winston/bunyan/roarr/tslog/consola/evlog/morgan/log4js — pino is the most-adopted in-category structured JSON logger, fastest, with child() context + redact). Shape: server-only src/lib/logger.ts; JSON to stdout in prod (Coolify/container aggregation), pino-pretty transport in dev; redact configured for token/secret fields (e.g. authorization, CF_EMAIL_TOKEN, invite codes). Scope: (1) the logger module; (2) replace db/client pool 'error' console.error with logger.error(err.message ...); (3) log-and-rethrow at the server-fn boundary. This is the base layer; wide-events/canonical-log-line request middleware is a separate follow-up that builds on it.
notes: Pulled ahead of P2: gf-fwi.2 now depends on this. A third caller — the dev email 'log' transport (decision 0013) — must route through the structured logger, not raw console. Sequence before P2's email wiring.

title: Wide-events request middleware (canonical log lines over pino)
description: Observability layer on top of the pino base logger (gf-fwi.10): emit ONE wide, structured 'canonical log line' per request instead of scattered log calls. Grounded in installed @tanstack/start-client-core 1.170 createMiddleware API.
design: Mechanism (verified against installed 1.170 source): use a REQUEST middleware — createMiddleware({type:'request'}).server(async ({request, pathname, next, handlerType, serverFnMeta}) => ...) — registered GLOBALLY via createStart({ requestMiddleware: [loggingMiddleware] }). Key facts: (1) request middleware fires for handlerType 'serverFn' AND 'router' (page/SSR), so one middleware covers both the server-fn data path and page loads — no separate Nitro hook needed for basic coverage. (2) Inputs for fields: raw web Request (method/headers/url), pathname, handlerType, serverFnMeta (fn name when a server fn). The middleware result exposes response (status). (3) Context: next({context:{log, reqId}}) injects the request-scoped pino child into server-fn context (typed via GlobalServerRequestContext); ALSO wrap next() in AsyncLocalStorage.run({log, fields}, ...) so services/db deep in the stack append fields without prop-drilling. (4) In a finally after next(), emit logger.info({reqId, handlerType, method, pathname, fn, status, durationMs, ...fields}, 'request'). (5) reqId sourcing: prefer an inbound correlation header, else generate — reqId = request.headers.get('cf-ray') ?? request.headers.get('x-request-id') ?? crypto.randomUUID(). Reusing Cloudflare's cf-ray correlates app logs with CF edge logs (the app is CF-fronted); crypto.randomUUID is zero-dep (ULID/nanoid only if time-sortable ids are later wanted). Prereq: project has NO Start instance yet (no src/start.ts) — this bead must add createStart + register the global request middleware. NOT pino-http (that's Node req/res; Start uses web Request/Response) — hand-roll with a pino child.
notes: Relationship to gf-fwi.10: the wide event absorbs the per-server-fn boundary log-and-rethrow (capture error outcome in the canonical line + rethrow), so avoid double-logging once this lands. Coverage caveat: truly raw Nitro routes (if any are ever added outside Start) bypass request middleware; negligible for this app. Depends on gf-fwi.10 (base pino logger).
